message.reasoning:
Let me assess the submission.

C1: Mission concept and rationale. Clear mission: coral reef monitoring satellite for Great Barrier Reef — sea surface temperature, thermal stress, bathymetry, colour/tone detection. Users: marine and conservation scientists, monitoring stations on ground. Rationale: bleaching events, 60% killed in 2016, 50% in 2017, ocean acidification 30%. References given (NOAA, NatGeo, DeepReef, Nature). This is Accomplished-level for rationale. However requirements/objectives are not clearly quantified (no explicit mission requirements list, e.g., resolution, revisit, coverage). Still "clear and complete description of mission goals, objectives, and requirements" — requirements are somewhat implicit. I'd say high Accomplished, maybe 8/10.

C2: Project plan — Gantt chart present, task descriptions, deadlines, weeks. Missing: contingency provision, references to information sources within the plan (sources listed in mission concept footnotes but not explicitly as "planned information sources" — the task requires listing information sources planned to use; these are cited sources for background, not a planned source list). No explicit contingency discussion. Also the plan is somewhat inconsistent: "Editing & Finalisation: Weeks 7 and 8 are reserved..." but Gantt shows editing in weeks 9 and 10. Contradiction. Also mission concept listed as complete in week 2-3 while Gantt shows only weeks 2-3 gold, fine. Background research gold through week 3 then blue weeks 4-8 — fine. So plan is presented with detail -> Adequate/Accomplished boundary. I'd say Adequate high, 6/10, or Accomplished low 7. Given lack of contingencies and source list and internal inconsistency, 6/10 (Adequate top).

C3: Preliminary progress — STK tutorials 1-4 completed, background research, Gantt, orbit "choice" of a geostationary orbit at 600 km which is technically wrong (GEO is ~35,786 km). No actual results/numerical analysis. That's minimal. Deficient-to-Adequate. Progress: reading, tutorials done, no design results. "Minor work completed" → Adequate low, 4/10. Perhaps 3/10 deficient? They do show some preliminary things but the only technical claim is wrong. I'd say 4/10 Adequate (low) — or 3. I'll go 4.

Hmm, the rubric for Accomplished C3: good preliminary results with interpretation. Not present. Adequate: minor work completed, results description insufficient. That fits: 4/10.

C4: Presentation — well-structured headings, readable, good writing, footnotes with URLs used as references (not proper formatting; numbered superscript footnotes at bottom). Figures: one Gantt chart labelled Image 1, described. References are just raw URLs — acceptable but not formal. Formatting consistent. Some references in text match list. Length ~2-3 pages. I'd say Accomplished low-mid: 7/10, since references are URLs not properly cited (but cited correctly-ish; in-text superscript numbers match footnote list). Actually in-text citations use superscript numbers that match the numbered list — good. But references lack titles/authors/dates. Also the software package requirement: STK chosen — mentioned as "STK Design & Simulations", "STK tutorials" — yes, STK is used. Software choice covered though not explicitly stated as a selection section.

I'd give C4 7/10.

Requirements:
R1: yes.
R2: partial — orbit/launch discussed at plan level, but orbit technical error (GEO at 600 km). Plan relates to space segment tasks (launch specifics, orbit specifics, ground control, comms, EOL). Partial because of incorrect orbit and little course material applied.
R3: yes — STK used (allowed).
R4: yes — Gantt chart.
R5: partial — sources given as footnotes for the background only, not a planned list of information sources. Actually the task says list information sources you plan to use; footnotes serve as sources used. Partial.
R6: partial — STK tutorials and research but no real results.

Technical issues:
- "geostationary orbit at an altitude of 600 km" — GEO altitude is 35,786 km; 600 km is LEO, cannot be geostationary and cannot stare at the reef continuously. Also revisit/coverage implications.
- 2017 "another 50 percent perished" — overstated; the 2017 bleaching affected the central section; combined 2016+2017 ~50% of shallow-water corals died. Claim as written is inaccurate.
- "Oceans have become 30 percent more acidic since the industrial revolution" — actually ocean pH has fallen 0.1 units, a ~30% increase in hydrogen ion concentration. Common phrasing; borderline. Could flag mildly.
- Resolution claim "current satellites have only mapped GBR depths to 100 m per pixel" — from deepreef; okay.
- No explicit mission requirements (spatial resolution, revisit, coverage, data latency, lifetime).
- Gantt inconsistency: editing weeks 9-10 vs text "weeks 7 and 8".
- No contingency.
- Mission concept complete in week 2-3 but background research ongoing; minor.
- End of life: "leaving it where it is" not compliant with debris guidelines; also GEO graveyard for 600 km is nonsense.

Let me write JSON.

Marks: C1 8/10 Accomplished; C2 6/10 Adequate; C3 4/10 Adequate; C4 7/10 Accomplished.

Overall summary ≤60 words.

Evidence quotes ≤25 words, contiguous.

C1 quote: "A near-real-time relay to monitoring stations on the ground would allow marine and conservation scientists to more accurately predict and react to coral bleaching events." That's 24 words? Count: A(1) near-real-time(2) relay(3) to(4) monitoring(5) stations(6) on(7) the(8) ground(9) would(10) allow(11) marine(12) and(13) conservation(14) scientists(15) to(16) more(17) accurately(18) predict(19) and(20) react(21) to(22) coral(23) bleaching(24) events(25). OK 25.

C2 quote: "Project work will be divided into weeks via a Gantt Chart. Detailed task descriptions can be found on the next page." Better: "...Deadlines are indicated by red lines." Use "Completed stages are gold. Incomplete stages are blue. Deadlines are indicated by red lines."

C3 quote: "completed STK tutorials 1, 2, 3 & 4" — full sentence: "Furthermore, in my progress, I have read the brief of Asner’s monitoring system in Hawaii, researched into how coral bleaching occurs and its severity, and also completed STK tutorials 1, 2, 3 & 4." Too long (>25). Use "researched into how coral bleaching occurs and its severity, and also completed STK tutorials 1, 2, 3 & 4." — count: researched1 into2 how3 coral4 bleaching5 occurs6 and7 its8 severity9 and10 also11 completed12 STK13 tutorials14 1,2,3,4=18. OK.

C4 quote: "Project work will be divided into weeks via a Gantt Chart." or "Detailed task descriptions can be found on the next page. Completed stages are gold." Use heading evidence: where "Project Plan & Preliminary Progress", quote "Completed stages are gold. Incomplete stages are blue. Deadlines are indicated by red lines."

For C2 quote use "Project work will be divided into weeks via a Gantt Chart."
